data.note:
Reflection: I called Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.70), truth is DNA damage for mitomycin C (PubChem CID 5746, ChEMBL DNA inhibitor).

Why I was wrong: 0.3-3 uM showed huge nuclear enlargement (nuc_area z 23-26, frac_large_nucleus z up to 9.5, nuc_dna_integrated z 5.6-14) with reduced cell count, which the atlas matched to Aurora references 3/4 NSC and 10/10 neighbours. I followed the NSC prior. But similarities were low ~0.55-0.65, i.e. weak evidence, and the high-dose tubulin brightening (tub_mean z 13, tub_glcm_contrast z 25) that the Microscopist called stabilization was a high-dose-only secondary effect (tub_mean rho +1.0 rising only at 10uM).

In hindsight the mid-dose phenotype - uniformly enlarged nuclei with increased integrated DNA, large spread cells, intact tubulin/actin, fewer mitotics - was exactly what the second Microscopist description suggested: DNA damage / DNA replication G2 arrest, not Aurora polyploidy. I down-weighted e12.

Literature supports true MoA: mitomycin C forms interstrand crosslinks that trigger checkpoint signaling even from a single crosslink (PMID 19748363), require UvrABC / translesion repair (PMID 20647419, PMID 20658647) and block replication of crosslink-containing DNA (PMID 34262911), producing G2 arrest and enlarged nuclei that can mimic Aurora polyploidy in morphology alone.

Lesson: when atlas similarity is low and per-well votes split by dose, prioritize multi-dose nuclear + DNA-content consistency and the Microscopist's cell-cycle read over a weak NSC majority, and require phospho-H3 / DNA-content flow to separate G2 arrest from failed cytokinesis.

reflection.text:
The nuclear measurements were correct but non-specific. nuc_area z=+23.6 to +26.7 with increased nuc_dna_integrated z=+14.0, frac_large_nucleus z=+9.5 and falling cell count rho=-1.0 across 0.3, 1 and 3 uM correctly identified arrest with enlarged, DNA-rich nuclei, and separating the 10 uM-only tubulin bundling (tub_mean z=+13.0 vs -2.7 to +1.0 at lower doses) from the primary phenotype was right.

What misled was over-weighting compare_to_reference_atlas e8 (NSC 3/4 Aurora, 10/10 neighbours) despite low similarities 0.55-0.60, and discounting describe_phenotype e12 which explicitly listed DNA damage and DNA replication at 1 uM. I treated enlarged nuclei as Aurora-specific and read the flat nuc_area dose-response rho=-0.20 as supportive rather than as early saturation, when mitomycin C interstrand crosslinks (PMID 17512921) trigger checkpoint arrest from even a single lesion (PMID 19748363) and block replication (PMID 34262911), producing the same enlargement.

Acquisition choices locked in the error: I spent all 4 wells on 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 uM with no low-dose 0.003-0.1 uM onset and no replicates, so I never tested the threshold or the H2AX vs phospho-H3 distinction that would have separated DNA-crosslink arrest from Aurora failure.
what_was_right: Detected huge reproducible nuclear enlargement across three independent doses (nuc_area z=+23.6, +26.4, +26.7) with increased integrated DNA and large-nucleus fraction, plus dose-dependent cell loss rho=-1.0
Correctly isolated high-dose-only tubulin effect at 10 uM (tub_glcm_contrast z=+25.1, tub_mean z=+13.0) from normal/low tubulin at 0.3-3 uM as secondary toxicity, not the primary MoA
Second microscopist description e12 naming DNA damage and DNA replication for the 1 uM large-nucleus phenotype pointed toward the true DNA inhibitor mechanism
what_was_wrong: Over-relied on NSC 3/4 and 10/10 neighbour vote for Aurora kinase inhibitors despite weak similarities 0.553-0.603, assigning 0.70 to Aurora vs 0.08 to DNA damage
Dismissed e12 DNA damage/replication visual call and e7 integrated DNA increase as generic enlargement instead of ICL checkpoint arrest

Misinterpreted flat nuc_area dose-response rho=-0.20 as consistency rather than saturation already at 0.3 uM, and failed to acquire low doses 0.003-0.1 uM or replicates to define onset and confirm specificity

citations.claim: Mitomycin C forms DNA interstrand crosslinks recognized by repair machinery (PMID 17512921).
A single DNA interstrand crosslink is sufficient to trigger checkpoint signaling and arrest (PMID 19748363).
Replication past interstrand crosslink-containing DNA requires coordinated cut and bypass repair (PMID 34262911).

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call is favored over runners-up by dose separation: at 0.3-3 uM (indices 4-6) nuc_area z=+23.6 to +26.7, frac_large_nucleus and integrated DNA rise, while tubulin is normal/low (tub_mean z=-2.7 to +1.0), arguing against microtubule stabilization except as a 10 uM-only effect (tub_mean z=+13.0, bundling on description). Acquisitions at 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 uM plus dose-response analyses were discriminative. No replicate is needed: the nuclear effect is huge and reproduced across three independent dose wells, and 0.70 appropriately leaves room for the discordant high-dose well.

## Unblinding

Compound: **mitomycin C** (PubChem CID [5746](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5746))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA damage**.

## Reflection

The nuclear measurements were correct but non-specific. nuc_area z=+23.6 to +26.7 with increased nuc_dna_integrated z=+14.0, frac_large_nucleus z=+9.5 and falling cell count rho=-1.0 across 0.3, 1 and 3 uM correctly identified arrest with enlarged, DNA-rich nuclei, and separating the 10 uM-only tubulin bundling (tub_mean z=+13.0 vs -2.7 to +1.0 at lower doses) from the primary phenotype was right.

What misled was over-weighting compare_to_reference_atlas e8 (NSC 3/4 Aurora, 10/10 neighbours) despite low similarities 0.55-0.60, and discounting describe_phenotype e12 which explicitly listed DNA damage and DNA replication at 1 uM. I treated enlarged nuclei as Aurora-specific and read the flat nuc_area dose-response rho=-0.20 as supportive rather than as early saturation, when mitomycin C interstrand crosslinks (PMID 17512921) trigger checkpoint arrest from even a single lesion (PMID 19748363) and block replication (PMID 34262911), producing the same enlargement.

Acquisition choices locked in the error: I spent all 4 wells on 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 uM with no low-dose 0.003-0.1 uM onset and no replicates, so I never tested the threshold or the H2AX vs phospho-H3 distinction that would have separated DNA-crosslink arrest from Aurora failure.

What was right:
- Detected huge reproducible nuclear enlargement across three independent doses (nuc_area z=+23.6, +26.4, +26.7) with increased integrated DNA and large-nucleus fraction, plus dose-dependent cell loss rho=-1.0
- Correctly isolated high-dose-only tubulin effect at 10 uM (tub_glcm_contrast z=+25.1, tub_mean z=+13.0) from normal/low tubulin at 0.3-3 uM as secondary toxicity, not the primary MoA
- Second microscopist description e12 naming DNA damage and DNA replication for the 1 uM large-nucleus phenotype pointed toward the true DNA inhibitor mechanism

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-relied on NSC 3/4 and 10/10 neighbour vote for Aurora kinase inhibitors despite weak similarities 0.553-0.603, assigning 0.70 to Aurora vs 0.08 to DNA damage
- Dismissed e12 DNA damage/replication visual call and e7 integrated DNA increase as generic enlargement instead of ICL checkpoint arrest
- Misinterpreted flat nuc_area dose-response rho=-0.20 as consistency rather than saturation already at 0.3 uM, and failed to acquire low doses 0.003-0.1 uM or replicates to define onset and confirm specificity

Proposed next experiment: Compare DNA-damage vs mitotic-failure markers at 0.3, 1 and 3 uM: gamma-H2AX/53BP1 foci and DNA-content flow for G2 arrest versus phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 and phospho-Aurora for Aurora inhibition, to test ICL-induced checkpoint arrest with enlarged 4N nuclei versus polyploidy from failed cytokinesis.
